en: Although many think Mount Mayon is the tallest, Mount Apo in Davao is actually the highest peak in the Philippines.
Many believe Palawan is part of the Visayas, but it is administratively classified under the Luzon island group.
Although often simplified, the Philippines is actually bordered by five major bodies of water, including the Celebes and Sulu Seas.
Many textbooks still state the Philippines has 7,107 islands, but updated national mapping reveals it actually consists of 7,641 islands.
While Laguna de Bay is the largest, Lake Lanao in Mindanao is actually the deepest lake in the Philippines.
Many assume the Pasig River is the longest due to its historical importance, but the Cagayan River holds that title.
Contrary to the belief that the country has four seasons, the Philippines only experiences two distinct seasons: wet and dry.
Many think Mount Pinatubo is still Luzon's highest peak, but the 1991 eruption lowered it, making Mount Pulag the tallest.
Although geographically situated in the Sulu Sea, the Tubbataha Reefs are administratively part of the Palawan province in Luzon.
Many believe the Philippine eagle is found only in Mindanao, but it also inhabits the forests of Luzon, Samar, and Leyte.
Although known as the Summer Capital, Baguio City is not the national capital, as that official title belongs to Manila.
Despite their name, the Chocolate Hills in Bohol are not made of cocoa, but consist of grass-covered limestone formations.
